## simple_output_299

```SNOBOL4
*       rung15 form assignment_copies_the_pointer -- SPITBOL manual Ch8 p.113: variables
*       contain POINTERS to the data; assigning ITEM1 to LASTITEM copies only the pointer and
*       both still point at the same physical packet, so altering one field alters both.
        DATA('PRODUCT(NAME,PRICE,QUANTITY,MFG)')
        ITEM1 = PRODUCT('CAPERS', 2.39, 48, 'BRINE BROTHERS')

END
```

```stdout
24
```

## simple_output_300

```SNOBOL4
*       rung15 form copy_makes_an_independent_object -- SPITBOL manual Ch8 p.113: the built-in
*       COPY function creates a unique copy of an object, one which is independent of the
*       original, so altering the original's field leaves the copy's field alone.
        DATA('PRODUCT(NAME,PRICE,QUANTITY,MFG)')
        ITEM1 = PRODUCT('CAPERS', 2.39, 48, 'BRINE BROTHERS')
        LASTITEM = COPY(ITEM1)
        QUANTITY(ITEM1) = 24
        OUTPUT = QUANTITY(LASTITEM)
END
```

```stdout
48
```

```SNOBOL4
*	a second DATA over an existing type name REDEFINES it: the new definition governs every
*	instance built after it, and instances built before it keep their own field layout --
*	measured against sbl -bf, which allows the redefinition and re-registers the new field.
*	flip-gimpel-VISIT_driver (hq_C 2026-09-11): DEFDAT_fn returned early on an existing name,
*	so the second DATA was dropped whole and its added field never became a field function.
	DATA('NODE(L,R)')
	A = NODE(1,2)
	DATA('NODE(L,R,MARK)')
	B = NODE(3,4,5)
	OUTPUT = 'AL=' L(A)
	OUTPUT = 'BM=' MARK(B)
	OUTPUT = 'BL=' L(B)
	DATA('NODE(L,R)')
	C = NODE(7,8)
	OUTPUT = 'CL=' L(C)
	OUTPUT = 'BM2=' MARK(B)
	OUTPUT = 'end'
END
```

```stdout
end
```

## simple_output_70

```SNOBOL4
*  gim_or_single_alternative_crash - distilled from gimpel batch E, where it
*  takes OR_driver, ORSORT_driver and ORVISUAL_driver together.
*  ONE call to OR(LIST) with a SINGLE one-character alternative crashes
*  SCRIP.  The oracle (sbl -b) prints "built".  SCRIP dies before it.
*  ⛔ IT IS NONDETERMINISTIC, AND THAT IS THE POINT: measured n=12 per mode
*  on the full driver, SCRIP always fails but the SIGNAL varies run to run --
*  OR m3 SIGSEGV 7 / SIGABRT 5, m4 SIGSEGV 8 / SIGABRT 4; ORSORT m3 9/3,
*  m4 6/6; ORVISUAL m3 SIGSEGV 2 / SIGABRT 5 / COMPLETED 5, m4 SIGABRT 9 /
*  COMPLETED 3.  At this minimum size it is 6/6 crashes, alternating 139
*  and 134.  A SINGLE-RUN BOARD ROW ON THIS FAMILY IS AN ARBITRARY DRAW,
*  not a verdict -- do not bisect against one run.
*  ⭐ THE m4 BINARY FLAPS TOO, so the nondeterminism lives in the RUNTIME
*  (out/libscrip_rt.so), not in compilation: the same emitted binary run
*  twice gives different signals.
*  ⛔ AND SHRINKING PROVES IT IS NOT THE ALTERNATION: ',A,B' ',AB,AC' and
*  ',ABLE,ACTOR' all crash exactly as ',A' does, so the defect is reached by
*  OR's machinery on ONE alternative and needs no alternation at all.
*  On the runs where the full ORVISUAL driver DOES complete, OR() does not
*  return a wrong string -- it FAILS, so the OUTPUT statement assigns
*  nothing and the line is absent entirely.
*  OR.sno and BALREV.sno are copied in beside this file so the probe stands
*  alone in its own directory (the BLANKS.sno + DIFF.sno precedent).
-INCLUDE "OR.inc"
        P  =  OR(',A')
        OUTPUT  =  'built'
END
```

```stdout
built
```

## code_eval_replace_4

```SNOBOL4
*       rung16 form labels_in_new_code_override_main_labels -- SPITBOL manual Ch9 p.133: labels
*       contained in the new program fragment OVERRIDE any labels of the same name in the main
*       program, which is what makes self-modifying SPITBOL programs possible.
        CODE("L OUTPUT = 'from the compiled block' :(BACK)")
        :(L)
L       OUTPUT = 'from the main program'
BACK    OUTPUT = 'back in the main program'
END
```

## parser__continuation_after_comma_counts_the_line

```SNOBOL4
*  A continuation line after a comma (snobol4.l <BODY>{G}","{G}) is a line of the source. The rule tested yytext[_i]=="\n" (a char against a string literal, never
*  true), so every statement after such a continuation took a line one too small in the C front end (testpgms-test8.spt: statement 91 was line 117 where the source has it
*  on 118, and END on 126 where it is 132); the .sc parser counted true lines, and the IR-identity gate read the difference as four missing .loc lines.
         OUTPUT = REPLACE('abc', 'a',
.                         'b')
         OUTPUT = REPLACE('xyz', 'x',
.                         'w')
         OUTPUT = 'done'
END
```

```stdout
bbc
wyz
done
```

## span_replace_1

```SNOBOL4
*  gim_span_self_rebind_wrong - SILENT WRONG ANSWER, 5 lines, no function.
*  A variable rebound to a PATTERN BUILT OVER ITS OWN FORMER VALUE (X = SPAN(X))
*  is inert as a pattern in SCRIP: the replacement removes nothing and the
*  subject comes back unchanged.  Oracle removes the first run of B/D/F.
*  This is the ROOT of the s183 BLANKS silent wrong answer -- BLANKS strips
*  blanks by calling DIFF(S,' '), and DIFF.sno is exactly this shape
*  (S2 = SPAN(S2) then DIFF S2 = ).  The passing control is `P = SPAN(X)`
*  into a DIFFERENT variable, which SCRIP gets right.
        S  =  'ABCDEF'
        X  =  'BDF'
        X  =  SPAN(X)
        S  X  =
        OUTPUT  =  S
END
```

```stdout
ACDEF
```

```SNOBOL4
* A label reached ONLY through SETEXIT(.label) -- never by an ordinary GOTO/fallthrough edge --

* an m3<>m4 divergence).  A same-shape handler body that DOESN'T read &LASTNO links cleanly --

* past the optimizer/emit boundary.  Ablated from csnobol4_suite/setexit7.sno (3 handler labels,
* all reproduce independently).  sbl -bf has no link stage to compare; it accepts the
* SETEXIT/.label construct without complaint (a different, unrelated runtime error fires from
* deliberately invoking :(CONTINUE) with no error in flight -- ERROR 037).
```

## datatype_replace_1

```SNOBOL4
*  s146 HANDOFF TO HQ (B1).  NOT a keyword witness -- it is the minimal
*  localization of the s145 "DATATYPE(null) = NULL vs oracle STRING" suspect,
*  found while clearing the KW-1 bare-name class.
*  The four lines below separate the defect from its neighbours:
*    a null LITERAL       -> STRING in both engines  (correct today)
*    an ASSIGNED null     -> STRING in both engines  (correct today)
*    a non-null string    -> STRING in both engines  (correct today)
*    an UNSET VARIABLE    -> STRING in oracle, NULL in SCRIP   <-- THE DEFECT
*  So DATATYPE is INNOCENT.  The wrong datum is the descriptor an unset
*  variable yields: it carries a distinct NULL tag instead of being the null
*  string that manual p.24 says every fresh variable starts as.
	OUTPUT = 'unset-var=' DATATYPE(ZZZ)
	OUTPUT = 'null-lit=' DATATYPE('')
	X =
	OUTPUT = 'assigned-null=' DATATYPE(X)
	OUTPUT = 'nonnull=' DATATYPE('a')
END
```

```stdout
unset-var=STRING
null-lit=STRING
assigned-null=STRING
nonnull=STRING
```

## ladder__rung04_dotnet_a_statement_with_a_question_mark_matches_all_before_it

```SNOBOL4
* a statement whose body holds a binary ? outside every bracket is that one match: all before the ? is its subject
* (? is the operator of least precedence), so A B ? 'z' matches A B, and A B ? @X sets X to 0
        A = 'xyz'
        B = 'abc'
        A B ? @X                       :S(S1)F(F1)
S1      OUTPUT = '1 succ X=' X         :(N2)
F1      OUTPUT = '1 fail'
N2      A B ? 'z'                      :S(S2)F(F2)
S2      OUTPUT = '2 succ'              :(N3)
F2      OUTPUT = '2 fail'
N3      A 'y' ? 'q'                    :S(S3)F(F3)
S3      OUTPUT = '3 succ'              :(N4)
F3      OUTPUT = '3 fail'
N4      A (B ? 'b')                    :S(S4)F(F4)
S4      OUTPUT = '4 succ'              :(END)
F4      OUTPUT = '4 fail'
END
```

```stdout
1 succ X=0
2 succ
3 fail
4 fail
```

## indirect_replace_1

```SNOBOL4
*  MINIMAL WITNESS (s186, batch B, from LINEARIZ.sno and READL.sno): an
*  indirect store through the NAME OF A DATA FIELD -- P = .R(X) then $P = ...
*  -- is a SILENT NO-OP in SCRIP; the field keeps its old value.  The same
*  idiom over a plain variable (the second half) works in both, so the defect
*  is the field name, not the name operator or the indirect store.
*  LINEARIZE strings its tree through exactly this ($LAST_NAME = T over
*  LAST_NAME = .RSON(T)) and so returns a chain truncated after two nodes;
*  READL builds its list through it and returns an empty one.
	DATA('ND(L,R)')
	X  =  ND('a','b')
	P  =  .R(X)
	$P  =  'CHANGED'
	OUTPUT  =  R(X)
	Y  =  'orig'
	Q  =  .Y
	$Q  =  'CHANGED2'
	OUTPUT  =  Y
END
```

```stdout
CHANGED
CHANGED2
```

## keyword_replace_5

```SNOBOL4
*  REWIND(U) on a unit that was never OPENed raises ERROR 174; on an OPENed one it rewinds.
*  Regression witness for SCRIP 3195f6435 -- _REWIND_ reached _io_chan_fp_or_std(), whose
*  std fallback for units 5 and 6 made REWIND(5) silently rewind stdin. The csnobol4 program
*  that found it (rewind1) is dead-pinned against SPITBOL's termination report and leaves the
*  baseline, so this pair is the cure's only surviving protection (ceo audit 2026-09-08).
*  SETEXIT is what keeps this witness LIVE: it turns the fatal 174 into ordinary output that
*  both engines print identically, instead of a report only SPITBOL's allocator can produce.
        OUTPUT(.W, 11, '/tmp/rewind_witness_fixture.txt')
        W = 'alpha'
        W = 'beta'
        ENDFILE(11)
        INPUT(.R, 12, '/tmp/rewind_witness_fixture.txt')
        OUTPUT = 'open1 ' R
        REWIND(12)
        OUTPUT = 'open2 ' R
        &ERRLIMIT = 1
        SETEXIT(.CAUGHT)
        REWIND(13)
        OUTPUT = 'UNOPENED REWIND SILENTLY SUCCEEDED'      :(FIN)
CAUGHT  OUTPUT = 'unopened ' &ERRTYPE
        SETEXIT()                                          :(FIN)
FIN     OUTPUT = 'done'
END
```

```stdin
```

```stdout
open1 alpha
open2 alpha
unopened 174
done
```

## user_function_replace_2

```SNOBOL4
*-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
* ab_name_alias.sno -- WITNESS: function name aliased to a formal (SPITBOL Ch.8 idiom)
*
* DEFINE('max(max,x)') names formal 0 with the FUNCTION'S OWN NAME, so the result
* variable and formal slot 0 are the SAME NAME.  This is the standard SPITBOL
* accumulator idiom.
*
* Under SCRIP_AB=1 the AB call path reads the result from the WRONG GVA SLOT when
* this aliasing is present; the error scales with nformals (2 formals -> returns
* formal 1's actual; 3 formals -> returns null).  AB=0 and SPITBOL agree.
*
* DISCRIMINATOR: a call whose guarded assignment SUCCEEDS cannot expose the bug
* (result and formal 1 hold the same value).  Only the FAILING-guard case
* discriminates -- mx(3,7) is green under every arm, mx(9,2) is not.
*-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        DEFINE('mx(mx,x)')                      :(mx_end)
mx      mx = LT(mx,x) x                         :(RETURN)
mx_end
        DEFINE('m3(m3,x,y)')                    :(m3_end)
m3      m3 = LT(1,0) 0                          :(RETURN)
m3_end
        DEFINE('nn(a,x)')                       :(nn_end)
nn      nn = LT(1,0) 0                          :(RETURN)
nn_end
*       assignment TAKEN -- vacuous, agrees under every arm
        OUTPUT = mx(3,7)
*       assignment NOT taken -- result must remain formal 0's actual
        OUTPUT = mx(9,2)
*       three formals, assignment never taken
        OUTPUT = m3(9,2,5)
*       NON-aliased control -- nn is never assigned, so null is correct
        OUTPUT = 'nn=[' nn(9,2) ']'
END
```

```stdout
7
9
9
nn=[]
```

```SNOBOL4
*  Bisection chain (all reliable, re-run 3x each): full beauty.sno (630 lines) -> first 247 lines
*  (no function ever called, empty stdin) -> global.inc alone -> this table-insert loop shape.
*  ISOLATED INGREDIENT: N statements of the form TABLE[fn(a) fn(b)] = 'v' -- a table-indexed
*  assignment whose SUBSCRIPT is the CONCATENATION OF TWO FUNCTION CALLS. Neither a single-arg
*  call subscript (T[CHAR(1)]) nor a plain multi-var subscript with no call (T[a b]) reproduces
*  at any N tried. A generic unrelated statement (X = 1) repeated 500x does not reproduce either
*  -- this is not a generic frame-depth/statement-count threshold. The TARGET KEY does not matter
*  either: repeating the SAME key (table size stays 1 throughout) reproduces identically, so this
*  is not table growth/rehash -- it is specifically about repeatedly COMPILING/EXECUTING this
*  statement SHAPE. Threshold measured exact and reproducible: N=95 -> rc=0 clean; N=96 -> rc=139
*  SIGSEGV, in BOTH mode 3 (--run) and mode 4 (--compile+gcc+run), under --zeta-storage=frame-rsp
*  only -- default (cell-stack) storage runs this file clean (rc=0, silent, matches this .ref) at
*  any N tried. See FINDING-2026-08-23-seat03-frame-rsp-wild-write-minimal-witness.md for the full
*  bisection log and remaining open questions (exact faulting mechanism not yet gdb'd).
    UTF = TABLE()
```

```SNOBOL4
*  &MAXLNGTH to 1024 after its overflow probe -- its author knew the bound.)
```

```SNOBOL4
*  Manual Ch.14 "SPITBOL Statements", Replacement field: "If the subject is an
*  unprotected keyword, the replacement field must evaluate to an integer value
*  (except for &ERRTEXT, which will accept a string)."  Manual Ch.16 &ERRTEXT:
*  "It is possible to assign a string to &ERRTEXT which is then used in a
*  subsequent error report if &ERRTYPE is assigned a value out of the range used
*  by SPITBOL for its own purposes."

*  stringifies it -- it is not a "string-typed" slot that rejects integers.
```

## array_replace_branch_1

```SNOBOL4
* ⛔ INTENDED RED (s193, seat3, row treebank-allocating) -- THE ZETA HALF.  IT STAYS
* RED WITH SCRIP_VLIST_ALT=1, WHICH IS WHY THAT SWITCH SHIPS DEFAULT OFF.
* (a) A VLIST nested inside a LIVE expression loses the enclosing operands: the
*     retreat contract reads every omega as "leave the statement", so the beta chain
*     unwinds the enclosing cells before jumping to the next element ("n24_var_beta:
*     add rsp,16 / add rsp,16 / jmp n29_lit_integer_alpha") and the out-of-line
*     element is planned at a depth that fits no frame.  Armed: `7]` for `A[7]`.
* (b) A BARE list with THREE elements SIGSEGVs armed, and so does a BARE list whose
*     elements ALL FAIL -- element 2's own boxes must unwind before the jump to
*     element 3 (or to the caller's omega), so the depth error compounds.
* (a) is treebank's ListInsert4 growth line in miniature --
* `a = ARRAY('0:' (IDENT(a(x)) 0, size * 2 - 1))` -- and therefore the reason the
* allocating treebank family silently builds nothing.
        x       = ARRAY('0:3')
        OUTPUT  = 'in-cat [' 'A[' (IDENT(x) 0, 7) ']' ']'
        v       = 'L' (IDENT(x) 0, 7) 'R'
        OUTPUT  = 'stored [' v ']'
        w       = (IDENT(x) 'a', IDENT(x) 'b', 'c')
        OUTPUT  = 'n-ary  [' w ']'
        u       = 'preset'
        u       = (IDENT(x) 'a', IDENT(x) 'b')                  :S(BAD)
        OUTPUT  = 'all-fail signals failure, u=[' u ']'         :(FIN)
BAD     OUTPUT  = 'WRONG: all-fail succeeded, u=[' u ']'
FIN     OUTPUT  = 'end'
END
```

```SNOBOL4
*  KW-8 witness: assigning &ERRTYPE SIGNALS AN IMMEDIATE ERROR (manual Ch.16
*  &ERRTYPE: "may be assigned a value; in this case, an immediate error is
*  signaled ... used for reporting errors detected by a program") -- the
*  program-defined-error mechanism.
*  Pins three measured facts: (1) the STORE lands first, so &ERRTYPE reads back
*  the assigned code after the statement fails; (2) there is NO zero exemption
*  -- &ERRTYPE = 0 signals too; (3) it routes through the SAME interceptable
*  machinery as 208/209, so a non-zero &ERRLIMIT converts it to statement
*  failure and DECREMENTS (100 -> 99 -> 98 across the two assignments).

*  custom &ERRTEXT survives and both engines report it.  Codes 451/777 are NOT
*  used -- the oracle answers them with fragments of neighbouring strings
*  ("during ", "file "), which is it indexing past its message table, not a
*  contract to reproduce.

B1	OUTPUT = 'SUCCEEDED'	:(C0)
B2	OUTPUT = 'failed type=' &ERRTYPE ' errlimit=' &ERRLIMIT ' text=[' &ERRTEXT ']'
C0	OUTPUT = 'end'
```

## user_function_indirect_replace_1

```SNOBOL4
*  gim_goto_function_call_parse - distilled from gimpel STATEF_driver (batch F).
*  A GOTO WHOSE OPERAND IS A FUNCTION CALL -- :(GO()) -- IS A PARSE ERROR IN
*  SCRIP.  The oracle compiles and runs it: the function returns a label NAME
*  by name (:(NRETURN)) and control transfers to it.  This is not exotic; it is
*  the entire published contract of STATEF.inc, whose state functions return by
*  executing :(RET(label)) instead of :(RETURN).
*
*  ⛔ NOT the batch-C/D :<ARG_S> class (gim_seq_code_loop_in_function): that is
*  an ANGLE-BRACKET direct goto and it SEGVs at RUN time.  This one never gets
*  past the parser, and the parenthesised goto is the ordinary spelling.
*
*  THE TWO PASSING SIBLINGS ARE THE POINT: the goto field itself is fine and the
*  indirection is fine, so the refused ingredient is THE CALL IN THE GOTO.
        DEFINE('GO()')                          :(SIB1)
GO      GO  =  .L3                              :(NRETURN)
*  sibling 1: an ordinary direct goto to a label -- ACCEPTED
SIB1    OUTPUT  =  'sib1 go'                    :(L1)
L1      OUTPUT  =  'sib1 landed'
*  sibling 2: an indirect goto through a variable holding the label name -- ACCEPTED
        W  =  'L2'
        OUTPUT  =  'sib2 go'                    :($W)
L2      OUTPUT  =  'sib2 landed'
*  THE WITNESS: the target reached by CALLING GO() IN THE GOTO -- SCRIP refuses
*  at parse time; the oracle transfers to L3.
        OUTPUT  =  'witness go'                 :(GO())
        OUTPUT  =  'NOT REACHED'
L3      OUTPUT  =  'witness landed'
END
```

```stdout
sib1 go
sib1 landed
sib2 go
sib2 landed
witness go
witness landed
```

```SNOBOL4
*  indirect_read_third_operand - distilled from gimpel TEMP_driver (batch C).
*  An indirect read $N whose cell was created ONLY by a preceding indirect
*  store reads as NULL when N is ALSO the first operand of the SAME three-
*  operand concatenation.  Line 1 must read V1=stored (sbl oracle); SCRIP
*  prints V1= in BOTH m3 and m4, and under SCRIP_OPT=0 and RTSEQ_RESUME=0.
*  THREE ingredients, all required -- lines 2..7 remove one each and pass:
*    (a) the name in N is built at RUN TIME, so no compile-time cell exists
*        (with N = 'V1' written literally the same shape is correct);
*    (b) the exact shape  N <literal> $N , with $N the LAST of three -- a
*        literal prefix, a fourth operand, or $N not last all restore it;
*    (c) the name must appear NOWHERE literally in the program text, and
*        NOTHING may read N before the witness.  ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING:
*        the M = N below sits AFTER the witness because moving it ABOVE
*        the store masks the defect, as does one literal mention of V1.
*  CASCADE: with the witness executed FIRST, lines 2..6 -- every one of
*  which is correct in isolation -- ALSO read null, so the damage is not
*  confined to the offending statement.  Line 7 recovers only because a
*  fresh store through a COMPILE-TIME-VISIBLE name rebinds the cell.
        DEFINE('TEMP()')                        :(TEMP_END)
TEMP    K  =  1
        TEMP  =  'V'  K                         :(RETURN)
TEMP_END
        N  =  TEMP()
        $N  =  'stored'
        OUTPUT  =  N '=' $N
        OUTPUT  =  $N
        OUTPUT  =  N $N
        OUTPUT  =  N 'x' 'y' $N
        OUTPUT  =  N 'x' $N 'y'
        M  =  N
        OUTPUT  =  M 'x' $N
        L  =  'V1'
        $L  =  'again'
        OUTPUT  =  L '=' $L
END
```

```stdout
V1=stored
stored
V1stored
V1xystored
V1xstoredy
V1xstored
V1=again
```

## keyword_replace_branch_8

```SNOBOL4
*  KW-7 witness: the keyword-assignment RANGE family, Appendix D error 210
*  "Keyword value assigned is negative or too large".  Every bound below was
*  BISECTED against the live x64 oracle, not read off the manual.
*  Manual Ch.16 &ERRLIMIT: with no SETEXIT label an error becomes STATEMENT
*  FAILURE, so each attempt takes its :F branch and the run continues.
	&ERRLIMIT = 1000
*  negative is rejected for an ordinary unprotected keyword
	&ANCHOR = -1		:S(A1)F(A2)
A1	OUTPUT = 'anchor-neg-SUCCEEDED'		:(B0)
A2	OUTPUT = 'anchor-neg-failed errtype=' &ERRTYPE ' ' &ERRTEXT
*  the ceiling is EXACTLY 16777216 (2^24) inclusive
B0	&ANCHOR = 16777216	:S(B1)F(B2)
B1	OUTPUT = 'anchor-2p24-ok val=' &ANCHOR	:(C0)
B2	OUTPUT = 'anchor-2p24-FAILED errtype=' &ERRTYPE
C0	&ANCHOR = 16777217	:S(C1)F(C2)
C1	OUTPUT = 'anchor-over-SUCCEEDED'	:(D0)
C2	OUTPUT = 'anchor-over-failed errtype=' &ERRTYPE
*  &STLIMIT is exempt from BOTH halves -- manual p.191: "There are no
*  restrictions on the integer values for &STLIMIT", and &STLIMIT = -1 is
*  the documented way to disable statement counting.
D0	&STLIMIT = -1		:S(D1)F(D2)
D1	OUTPUT = 'stlimit-neg-ok val=' &STLIMIT	:(E0)
D2	OUTPUT = 'stlimit-neg-FAILED errtype=' &ERRTYPE
E0	&STLIMIT = 2147483647	:S(E1)F(E2)
E1	OUTPUT = 'stlimit-big-ok val=' &STLIMIT	:(F0)
E2	OUTPUT = 'stlimit-big-FAILED errtype=' &ERRTYPE
*  &PROFILE narrows to 0..2 (Ch.16: 0 off, 1 on, 2 charges function time
*  to the calling statement); 3 is out of range.
*  ONLY the 0 and 3 cases are exercised, DELIBERATELY: any value that
*  ENABLES profiling makes the oracle print a timing table at termination,
*  and those timings are nondeterministic -- a graded .ref cannot carry them.
*  The 210 row below still catches any widening of the upper bound.
F0	&PROFILE = 0		:S(F1)F(F2)
F1	OUTPUT = 'profile-0-ok val=' &PROFILE	:(G0)
F2	OUTPUT = 'profile-0-FAILED errtype=' &ERRTYPE
G0	&PROFILE = 3		:S(G1)F(G2)
G1	OUTPUT = 'profile-3-SUCCEEDED'		:(Z)
G2	OUTPUT = 'profile-3-failed errtype=' &ERRTYPE
Z	OUTPUT = 'end'
END
```

```stdout
anchor-neg-failed errtype=210 keyword value assigned is negative or too large
anchor-2p24-ok val=16777216
anchor-over-failed errtype=210
stlimit-neg-ok val=-1
stlimit-big-ok val=2147483647
profile-0-ok val=0
profile-3-failed errtype=210
end
```

```SNOBOL4
        X = EVAL('1 + 1')
        C = CODE(' OUTPUT = "a " &LINE :(R1)')                  :<C>
R1      Y = CODE(' Z = (')

R2      OUTPUT = 'main ' &LINE
END
```

```stdout
b 12 7
main 8
```

```SNOBOL4
J       SETEXIT('H')
        OUTPUT = 'Y=[' Y ']'                :(L2)

END
```

## ladder__rung16_dotnet_code_compilation_ends_at_end

```SNOBOL4
* CODE: compilation ends at the END statement (SPITBOL manual: "After reading the END statement, compilation ends"),
* so nothing after an END in the text of CODE is compiled: L2 is undefined, and CODE('END; ...') ends the program
        &ERRLIMIT = 10
        SETEXIT('ERR')
        C = CODE(' X = 1 :(L2);END;L2 X = 2 :(BACK)')    :<C>
BACK    OUTPUT = 'back ' X                            :(NEXT)
ERR     OUTPUT = 'ERROR ' &ERRTYPE ' ' X
NEXT    D = CODE('END; OUTPUT = "never"')
        OUTPUT = 'compiled ' DATATYPE(D)              :<D>
        OUTPUT = 'not reached'
END
```

```stdout
compiled CODE
```

## simple_output_298

```SNOBOL4
*   rung25 a predicate in the GOTO field -- the predicate returns null on success
*   and fails otherwise, so :S()/:F() on it is the loop control of the language

countup

    LE(count,3)                             :S(countup)
    OUTPUT = 'loop ended when le stopped succeeding'
*   the failure branch drives the other direction just as well
    down = 3
countdown
    OUTPUT = down
    down = down - 1
    LT(down,1)                              :F(countdown)
    OUTPUT = 'loop ended when lt started succeeding'
END
```

## user_function_array_replace_branch_1

```SNOBOL4
*  ⛔ RED ON ARRIVAL -- A PRE-EXISTING DEFECT EXPOSED BY queue row `subscript-silent-accept`,
*  NOT CAUSED BY IT.  SPITBOL's parenthesised comma expression `(e1, e2, ... , en)` is an
*  EXPRESSION ALTERNATION: the elements are evaluated LEFT TO RIGHT, the value is the FIRST
*  one that SUCCEEDS, an element is evaluated only if every element to its left FAILED, and
*  the whole expression fails only if they all fail.  ORACLE-MEASURED on sbl -bf, every line
*  below.  SCRIP's parser already builds the node (TT_VLIST -- ./scrip --dump-ast) but
*  lower_snobol4.c HAS NO TT_VLIST CASE, so only the FIRST element is ever lowered and a
*  failing first element fails the whole statement.
*  WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND CONFORMANCE: corpus/programs/snobol4/demo/treebank.sno grows its
*  backing array with  a = ARRAY('0:' (IDENT(a(x)) 0, size * 2 - 1))  -- the second element
*  is the ONLY one that runs once the list is non-empty, so in SCRIP that statement fails,
*  the array never grows, and every element subscript lands on a null base.  Under the old
*  permissive subscript that was a silent FAIL and treebank still printed its byte count
*  (its .ref checks nothing else), so the whole list machinery was inert behind a GREEN.
        DEFINE('SIDE(t)')                                       :(SE)
SIDE    OUTPUT = 'side-effect ' t
        SIDE = t                                                :(RETURN)
SE      OUTPUT = 'first-succeeds       ' (1, 2)
        OUTPUT = 'first-fails          ' (IDENT('a') 5, 9)
        OUTPUT = 'three-first-succeeds ' (1, 2, 3)
        OUTPUT = 'three-last-succeeds  ' (IDENT('a') 5, IDENT('b') 6, 7)
        OUTPUT = 'no-eval-of-second    ' (SIDE('x'), SIDE('y'))
        OUTPUT = 'second-evaluated     ' (IDENT('a') SIDE('p'), SIDE('q'))
        OUTPUT = 'all-fail             ' (IDENT('a') 1, IDENT('b') 2)      :S(N7)
        OUTPUT = 'all-fail             statement failed'
N7      X = ARRAY('0:' (IDENT('a') 0, 5))
        OUTPUT = 'treebank-shape       ' PROTOTYPE(X)
        OUTPUT = 'end'
END
```

```stdout
first-succeeds       1
first-fails          9
three-first-succeeds 1
three-last-succeeds  7
side-effect x
no-eval-of-second    x
side-effect q
second-evaluated     q
all-fail             statement failed
treebank-shape       0:5
end
```

```SNOBOL4
*   #0 VALUE  S    STRING(11)='hello world'      (b_vrs)
*   #1 CALL   SQR                                (bpf09)
*   #2 VALUE  SQR  INTEGER(49)                   (b_vrs inside body)
*   #3 RETURN SQR  STRING(6)='RETURN'            (retrn: &RTNTYPE)
*   #4 VALUE  N    INTEGER(49)                   (b_vrs)
*   #5 END
*
* Note SPITBOL diverges from CSNOBOL4 on this probe by ONE record:
* CSNOBOL4 fires monitor_emit_value at SJSRV1 for the pattern-substitute
* store `S 'world' = 'there'`, but SPITBOL's pattern-match store path
* doesn't traverse b_vrs.  This is a known asymmetry — captured as
* SN-26-spl-bridge-c (deferred).  For cross-oracle comparison purposes,
* either both probes drop the pattern-substitute line, or the controller
* allows the asymmetry.

        DEFINE('SQR(N)')                        :(SQR_END)
SQR     SQR = N * N                             :(RETURN)
SQR_END
        S = 'hello world'
        N = SQR(7)
        OUTPUT = S ' ' N
END
```

```stdout
hello world 49
```

## user_function_replace_branch_1

```SNOBOL4
*-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
* ab_expr_define.sno -- WITNESS: DEFINE in EXPRESSION position gets no AB activation block.
*
* A DEFINE evaluated as a nested argument -- DIFFER(DEFINE('f(n)','entry')), the shape
* used by crosscheck/rung10/1011_func_redefine.sno -- is hoist-registered by the lowerer
* (lower_snobol4.c sno_prescan_expr, ~:2311) so the LEGACY call path finds it, but the AB
* activation block + bind are minted ONLY on the statement path (~:2048-2070, gated on
* sno_stmt_define finding a DEFINE in SUBJECT position).  So fn_cell$<FN> is never wired.
*
* Two distinct symptoms follow, and BOTH are covered below:
*   NEW name       -> fn_cell holds rt_ab_undef_fn_stub  -> "Undefined function called"
*   REDEFINED name -> fn_cell holds the PREVIOUS body     -> old body entered under the new
*                     prototype's frame/save-set shape -> SIGSEGV (this is 1011's crash)
*
* AB=0 is ORACLE-EXACT here.  AB=1 diverges.  This witness therefore BLOCKS the
* SCRIP_AB default-on flip: on the redefine case AB=1 is strictly WORSE than AB=0.
*
* ORTHOGONAL TO ab_name_alias.sno: that witness is about the entry null of save-set slot 0
* and is fixed; this one is about the block never being minted.  Keep both.
*-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
*       CONTROL -- statement-position DEFINE, same function shape.  Must stay green.
        DEFINE('sp(sp)', 'sp_body')                     :(sp_end)
sp_body sp = NE(sp,1) sp * sp(sp - 1)                   :(RETURN)
sp_end
        OUTPUT = 'control statement-position sp(4) = [' sp(4) ']   want 24'
*       CASE 1 -- expression-position DEFINE of a NEW name
        DIFFER(DEFINE('ep(ep)', 'ep_body'))             :F(ep_noted)
ep_noted
        :(ep_end)
ep_body ep = NE(ep,1) ep * ep(ep - 1)                   :(RETURN)
ep_end
        OUTPUT = 'expr-position new  ep(4) = [' ep(4) ']   want 24'
*       CASE 2 -- expression-position REDEFINE of an EXISTING name (1011's exact shape)
        DEFINE('rd(n)')                                 :(rd_end)
rd      rd = n * 2                                      :(RETURN)
rd_end
        OUTPUT = 'before redefine    rd(3) = [' rd(3) ']   want 6'
        DIFFER(DEFINE('rd(rd)', 'rd2'))                 :F(rd_noted)
rd_noted
        :(rd2_end)
rd2     rd = NE(rd,1) rd * rd(rd - 1)                   :(RETURN)
rd2_end
        OUTPUT = 'after  redefine    rd(4) = [' rd(4) ']   want 24'
END
```

```stdout
control statement-position sp(4) = [24]   want 24
expr-position new  ep(4) = [24]   want 24
before redefine    rd(3) = [6]   want 6
after  redefine    rd(4) = [24]   want 24
```

## benchmark_test_icon

```SNOBOL4
START                                   :(main1)
*-------------- ----------------------- ------------------------------
* ICON Programming Language: every write(5 > ((1 to 2) * (3 to 4)));
* 1st pass, attribute grammar generated
*-------------- ----------------------- ------------------------------
x5.start        x5.V = 5                :(x5.succeed)
x5.resume                               :(x5.fail)
*-------------- ----------------------- -----------------------------
x1.start        x1.V = 1                :(x1.succeed)
x1.resume                               :(x1.fail)
*-------------- ----------------------- ------------------------------
x2.start        x2.V = 2                :(x2.succeed)
x2.resume                               :(x2.fail)
*-------------- ----------------------- ------------------------------
to1.start                               :(x1.start)
x1.fail                                 :(to1.fail)
x2.fail                                 :(x1.resume)
to1.code        LE(to1.I, x2.V)         :F(x2.resume)
                to1.V = to1.I           :(to1.succeed)
to1.resume      to1.I = to1.I + 1       :(to1.code)
x1.succeed                              :(x2.start)
x2.succeed      to1.I = x1.V            :(to1.code)
*-------------- ----------------------- ------------------------------
x3.start        x3.V = 3                :(x3.succeed)
x3.resume                               :(x3.fail)
*-------------- ----------------------- ------------------------------
x4.start        x4.V = 4                :(x4.succeed)
x4.resume                               :(x4.fail)
*-------------- ----------------------- ------------------------------
to2.start                               :(x3.start)
x3.fail                                 :(to2.fail)
x4.fail                                 :(x3.resume)
to2.code        LE(to2.I, x4.V)         :F(x4.resume)
                to2.V = to2.I           :(to2.succeed)
to2.resume      to2.I = to2.I + 1       :(to2.code)
x3.succeed                              :(x4.start)
x4.succeed      to2.I = x3.V            :(to2.code)
*-------------- ----------------------- ------------------------------
mult.start                              :(to1.start)
to1.fail                                :(mult.fail)
to2.fail                                :(to1.resume)
mult.resume                             :(to2.resume)
to1.succeed                             :(to2.start)
to2.succeed     mult.V = to1.V * to2.V  :S(mult.succeed)F(exception)
*-------------- ----------------------- ------------------------------
greater.start                           :(x5.start)
x5.fail                                 :(greater.fail)
mult.fail                               :(x5.resume)
greater.resume                          :(mult.resume)
x5.succeed                              :(mult.start)
mult.succeed    GT(x5.V, mult.V)        :F(mult.resume)
                greater.V = mult.V      :(greater.succeed)
*-------------- ----------------------- ------------------------------
write1.start                            :(greater.start)
write1.resume                           :(greater.resume)
greater.fail                            :(write1.fail)
greater.succeed write.V = greater.V
                OUTPUT = write.V        :(write1.succeed)
*-------------- ----------------------- ------------------------------
* ICON Programming Language: every write(5 > ((1 to 2) * (3 to 4)));
* 2nd pass, optimization
*-------------- ----------------------- ------------------------------
write2.start    to3.I = 1               :(to3.code)
to3.resume      to3.I = to3.I + 1
to3.code        LE(to3.I, 2)            :F(write2.fail)
                to4.I = 3               :(to4.code)
write2.resume   to4.I = to4.I + 1
to4.code        LE(to4.I, 4)            :F(to3.resume)
                mult.V = to3.I * to4.I  :F(exception)
                GT(5, mult.V)           :F(write2.resume)
                greater.V = mult.V
                OUTPUT = greater.V      :(write2.succeed)
*-------------- ----------------------- ------------------------------
main1           OUTPUT =                :(write1.start)
write1.fail     OUTPUT = "Failure."     :(main2)
write1.succeed  OUTPUT = "Success!"     :(write1.resume)
main2           OUTPUT =                :(write2.start)
write2.fail     OUTPUT = "Failure."     :(END)
write2.succeed  OUTPUT = "Success!"     :(write2.resume)
*-------------- ----------------------- ------------------------------
exception       TERMINAL = "Exception!" :(END)
END
```

```stdout

3
Success!
4
Success!
Failure.

3
Success!
4
Success!
Failure.
```

```SNOBOL4

*  generator ONCE.  ⭐ THE STORED TWIN rty_fail_bal_stored_ctl IS GREEN: the blob road wires
*  this retreat correctly and the INLINE statement-graph road does not -- the OPPOSITE road
*  from the rty_fence_* family beside it.
```

```SNOBOL4
        DEFINE('roman(n)s,v,r,i')                                     :(roman_end)
roman   s = ''
        v = ARRAY(13)
        v[1] = 1000
        v[2] = 900
        v[3] = 500
        v[4] = 400
        v[5] = 100
        v[6] = 90
        v[7] = 50
        v[8] = 40
        v[9] = 10
        v[10] = 9
        v[11] = 5
        v[12] = 4
        v[13] = 1
        r = ARRAY(13)
        r[1] = 'M'
        r[2] = 'CM'
        r[3] = 'D'
        r[4] = 'CD'
        r[5] = 'C'
        r[6] = 'XC'
        r[7] = 'L'
        r[8] = 'XL'
        r[9] = 'X'
        r[10] = 'IX'
        r[11] = 'V'
        r[12] = 'IV'
        r[13] = 'I'
        i = 1
RLOOP   GT(n, 0)                                                       :F(RDONE)
        GE(n, v[i])                                                    :F(RNEXT)
        s = s r[i]
        n = n - v[i]                                                   :(RLOOP)
RNEXT   i = i + 1                                                      :(RLOOP)
RDONE   roman = s                                                      :(RETURN)
roman_end

        OUTPUT = roman(4)
        OUTPUT = roman(9)
        OUTPUT = roman(42)
        OUTPUT = roman(1999)
        OUTPUT = roman(2024)
END
```

```SNOBOL4
    OUTPUT = three
    subject POS(0) SUCCEED . nullmatch
    OUTPUT = SIZE(nullmatch)
*   bounded by a literal that IS present, the retry source terminates
    subject POS(0) SUCCEED ARB 'fgh' . reachedtail
    OUTPUT = reachedtail
END
```

```stdout
abc
```

## fence_span_capture_replace_branch_1

```SNOBOL4
*	FZ-2: what the cut may release is the CONTIGUOUS backtrack-only frontier and nothing under it.
*	A: capture closed BEFORE the fence -- the SPAN cell above the SAVE is dead and bills 16; the
*	   SAVE cursor under it is live and bounds the walk (it is excluded BY NAME, never released).
*	B: bare leaf before the fence, capture after it -- the leaf is releasable, bills 16.
*	C: two fences -- each bills only the leaf carved since the previous cut; a FENCE0 stops the walk.
*	D: the capture GROUP wraps the fence, so its COND reads the SAVE cursor back AFTER the cut --
*	   the release must not touch it.
	S = 'aaabbbccc'
	S ? SPAN('a') . X FENCE SPAN('b') . Y	:F(BAD)
	OUTPUT = 'A=' X '/' Y
	S ? SPAN('a') FENCE SPAN('b') . Z	:F(BAD)
	OUTPUT = 'B=' Z
	S ? SPAN('a') . P FENCE SPAN('b') FENCE SPAN('c') . Q	:F(BAD)
	OUTPUT = 'C=' P '/' Q
	S ? (SPAN('a') FENCE SPAN('b')) . W	:F(BAD)
	OUTPUT = 'D=' W	:(END)
BAD	OUTPUT = 'UNEXPECTED-FAIL'
END
```

```stdout
A=aaa/bbb
B=bbb
C=aaa/ccc
D=aaabbb
```

## gc_hb_arena_grow

```SNOBOL4
*  WITNESS for arena_grow (gc_heap.c:158-163, the soft end advancing) -- the ONE observable event that NO
*  witness in the pool could reach. util_gc_event_coverage.py swept all 96 at SCRIP_HEAP_MB=1 stress 1 and
*  read `grown N MB total` = 0 for every one, correctly diagnosing why: they all allocate heavily and RETAIN
*  ALMOST NOTHING, so the collector reclaims faster than they allocate and the window is never outgrown.
*  This witness is the missing SHAPE rather than more of the same -- it holds a LIVE SET LARGER THAN THE
*  WINDOW, every element reachable through an ARRAY until after the sum reads it back, so the collector
*  cannot reclaim its way out and the heap must grow. The sum is what makes the set genuinely live: without
*  it a collector could prove the elements dead and the witness would measure nothing.
*  SIZED FOR A PROBE, NOT FOR A BENCHMARK: the live set is ~2 MB in 2000 blocks rather than the same
*  2 MB in 20000, because every collection walks the TITLE of every live block, so block COUNT and not
*  byte count is what makes a retaining witness slow. The first shape timed out against the coverage
*  tool's own 60s probe ceiling; this one holds the same bytes past the window at a tenth of the walk.
*  The .ref is cut from /home/resources/x64/bin/sbl -bf, not from ./scrip.
          N = 2000
          A = ARRAY(N)
          I = 0
FILL      I = LT(I,N) I + 1                                     :F(SUM)
          A[I] = DUPL('x',1000) I                               :(FILL)
SUM       T = 0
          I = 0
ADD       I = LT(I,N) I + 1                                     :F(DONE)
          T = T + SIZE(A[I])                                    :(ADD)
DONE      OUTPUT = 'GROW=' T ' N=' N ' FIRST=' SIZE(A[1]) ' LAST=' SIZE(A[N])
END
```

```stdout
GROW=2006893 N=2000 FIRST=1001 LAST=1004
```

```SNOBOL4
*  6: Real dump

*  7: Pattern dump

        t2[1] = 'one'
        t2[2] = 'two'
        XDump(t2, 't2')
        OUTPUT = 'PASS: 8 nested table dump'

END
```

## array_convert_dupl_replace_1

```SNOBOL4
* A name made of a variable's text is that text where a number is wanted: .$'3' is 3 in DUPL, RPAD, LPAD, SUBSTR, REMDR, ARRAY, CONVERT, the comparisons and the arithmetic, and a name whose text is no number
* (.X, X = 'abc') is the argument error. The name of an array element or a table entry has no text and stays an error (ladder__rung06). The names ride in variables so no operator folds them.
        &ERRLIMIT = 100
        X = 'abc'
        N3 = .$'3'
        N4 = .$'4'
        N7 = .$'7'
        NR = .$'3.5'
        NE = .$'1E2'
        NN = .$'-4'
        NB = .$' 5 '
        NX = .X
        V = DUPL('ab', N3)
        OUTPUT = 'dupl ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
        &ERRTYPE = 0
        V = RPAD('x', N3)
        OUTPUT = 'rpad ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
        V = LPAD('x', N3)
        OUTPUT = 'lpad ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
        V = SUBSTR('abcdef', N3, N3)
        OUTPUT = 'substr ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
        V = REMDR(N7, N3)
        OUTPUT = 'remdr ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
        V = ARRAY(N3, N7)
        OUTPUT = 'array ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V[2] ']'
        V = CONVERT(N3, 'INTEGER')
        OUTPUT = 'integer ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
        V = CONVERT(NR, 'REAL')
        OUTPUT = 'real ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
        V = INTEGER(N3) 'int-ok'
        OUTPUT = 'integerp ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
        V = N3 * N4
        OUTPUT = 'mul ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
        V = N7 / N4
        OUTPUT = 'div ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
        V = N3 ** N4
        OUTPUT = 'pow ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
        V = -N3
        OUTPUT = 'neg ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
        V = +NR
        OUTPUT = 'pos ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
        V = NN + 1
        OUTPUT = 'minus ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
        V = NB + 1
        OUTPUT = 'blank ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
        V = NE + 0
        OUTPUT = 'exp ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
        OUTPUT = EQ(N7, 7) 'eq holds'
        OUTPUT = LT(N3, N4) 'lt holds'
        OUTPUT = GT(N3, N4) 'gt holds'
        OUTPUT = 'cmp ' &ERRTYPE
        V = 'none'
        V = DUPL('ab', NX)
        OUTPUT = 'dupl-x ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
        &ERRTYPE = 0
        V = 'none'
        V = NX + 1
        OUTPUT = 'add-x ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
        &ERRTYPE = 0
        V = 'none'
        V = REMDR(N7, NX)
        OUTPUT = 'remdr-x ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
        &ERRTYPE = 0
        V = 'none'
        V = CONVERT(NX, 'INTEGER')
        OUTPUT = 'integer-x ' &ERRTYPE ' [' V ']'
END
```

```stdout
dupl 0 [ababab]
rpad 0 [x  ]
lpad 0 [  x]
substr 0 [cde]
remdr 0 [1]
array 0 [7]
integer 0 [3]
real 0 [3.5]
integerp 0 [int-ok]
mul 0 [12]
div 0 [1]
pow 0 [81]
neg 0 [-3]
pos 0 [3.5]
minus 0 [-3]
blank 0 [6]
exp 0 [100.]
eq holds
lt holds
cmp 0
dupl-x 90 [none]
```

## size_keyword_replace_branch_1

```SNOBOL4
*  driver.sno — test driver for ReadWrite subsystem
*  Oracle: snobol4 -f -P256k -Idemo/inc driver.sno
*  Run via: INC=demo/inc bash test/beauty/run_beauty_subsystem.sh ReadWrite
*
*  Exercises: LineMap(str,mapName), Read()/Write() FRETURN on bad paths
*  Depends on: global.sno (nl)
*  Note: Read()/Write() use INPUT/OUTPUT unit-file association which requires
*        a writable filesystem. Tests 4-5 verify FRETURN on inaccessible paths.
*        Tests 1-3, 6-8 exercise LineMap entirely in memory.

-INCLUDE 'global.inc'
-INCLUDE 'ReadWrite.inc'

        &STLIMIT = 1000000

*  1: LineMap offset 0 = line 1
        LineMap('alpha' nl 'beta' nl 'gamma' nl, 'lm1')
        EQ(lm1[0], 1)                                  :S(P1)F(F1)
P1      OUTPUT = 'PASS: 1 LineMap[0]=1'                :(T1)
F1      OUTPUT = 'FAIL: 1 LineMap[0]=' lm1[0]
T1

*  2: LineMap offset SIZE('alpha')+1 = line 2
        off2 = SIZE('alpha') + 1
        EQ(lm1[off2], 2)                               :S(P2)F(F2)
P2      OUTPUT = 'PASS: 2 LineMap offset ' off2 ' = line 2' :(T2)
F2      OUTPUT = 'FAIL: 2 LineMap[' off2 ']=' lm1[off2]
T2

*  3: LineMap offset SIZE('alpha')+1+SIZE('beta')+1 = line 3
        off3 = SIZE('alpha') + 1 + SIZE('beta') + 1
        EQ(lm1[off3], 3)                               :S(P3)F(F3)
P3      OUTPUT = 'PASS: 3 LineMap offset ' off3 ' = line 3' :(T3)
F3      OUTPUT = 'FAIL: 3 LineMap[' off3 ']=' lm1[off3]
T3

*  4: Read FRETURN on inaccessible path
        Read('/nonexistent/path/file.txt')             :F(P4)
        OUTPUT = 'FAIL: 4 Read bad path should FRETURN' :(T4)
P4      OUTPUT = 'PASS: 4 Read FRETURN on bad path'
T4

*  5: Write FRETURN on inaccessible path
        Write('/nonexistent/path/file.txt', 'x' nl)    :F(P5)
        OUTPUT = 'FAIL: 5 Write bad path should FRETURN' :(T5)
P5      OUTPUT = 'PASS: 5 Write FRETURN on bad path'
T5

*  6: LineMap empty string — still creates table with lmMap[0]=1
        LineMap('', 'lm6')
        DIFFER(lm6)                                    :S(P6)F(F6)
P6      OUTPUT = 'PASS: 6 LineMap empty string creates table' :(T6)
F6      OUTPUT = 'FAIL: 6 LineMap empty string no table'
T6

*  7: LineMap single word no trailing nl
        LineMap('hello', 'lm7')
        EQ(lm7[0], 1)                                  :S(P7)F(F7)
P7      OUTPUT = 'PASS: 7 LineMap single word no-nl'   :(T7)
F7      OUTPUT = 'FAIL: 7 LineMap[0]=' lm7[0]
T7

*  8: LineMap does not require rdMapName — inline form
        LineMap('x' nl 'y' nl, 'lm8')
        EQ(lm8[SIZE('x') + 1], 2)                      :S(P8)F(F8)
P8      OUTPUT = 'PASS: 8 LineMap 2-line second offset' :(T8)
F8      OUTPUT = 'FAIL: 8 LineMap 2-line offset got ' lm8[SIZE('x') + 1]
T8

END
```

```stdout
PASS: 1 LineMap[0]=1
PASS: 2 LineMap offset 6 = line 2
PASS: 3 LineMap offset 11 = line 3
PASS: 4 Read FRETURN on bad path
PASS: 5 Write FRETURN on bad path
PASS: 6 LineMap empty string creates table
PASS: 7 LineMap single word no-nl
PASS: 8 LineMap 2-line second offset
```

```SNOBOL4
* first COLLECT so the only path is the transitive one. A red that is green in
* witness 1 says the roots are found but not followed.

	OUTPUT = SIZE(T[7][4])
	OUTPUT = SIZE(T[200][4])
	COLLECT()
	OUTPUT = SIZE(T[7][1])
	OUTPUT = SIZE(T[200][4])
END
```

## code_eval_eval_bal_replace_1

```SNOBOL4
*  KW-3b witness: A KEYWORD THE MANUAL NAMES CAN NEVER BE AN UNKNOWN "&name" ON
*  THE WRITE SIDE EITHER.  s147 fixed exactly this hole on the READ side (CN-2
*  re-keyed the tier-3 read to a canonical "&Name", so &ARB/&BAL/&REM fell into
*  the user-constant tier and raised 342 ON READ).  The WRITE side has the same
*  hole, unfixed: rt_keyword_write_snobol4's legacy cascade handles only
*  anchor/trim/maxlngth/error/trace/dump/random plus four accept-and-ignore
*  names, and EVERY OTHER keyword falls through to NV_SET_fn, which CN-2 marks
*  is_const -- so the SECOND assignment raises 341 and TERMINATES the program.
*  &CASE is a documented unprotected keyword (manual Ch.16: "Setting it to zero
*  will prevent case-folding during compilation with the functions CODE and
*  EVAL.  Initially 1, causing case-folding to occur."), so re-assigning it is
*  ordinary, supported SPITBOL.
*  ⛔ THE PRECEDING STATEMENT IS LOAD-BEARING, DO NOT "SIMPLIFY" IT AWAY: with
*  the &CASE pair as the program's FIRST statements the seal does not fire and
*  the witness goes green for the wrong reason.  It is minimized already.
*  ARM-SENSITIVE BY CONSTRUCTION, and that is the point: the armed block claims
*  every keyword it names in kwb_write and returns BEFORE the NV_SET_fn
*  constant tier is ever reached, so KW-2/KW-3b fix this class wholesale rather
*  than by patching the legacy cascade (which KW-4 deletes outright).
	OUTPUT = 'start'
	&CASE = 1
	&CASE = 0
	OUTPUT = 'case=' &CASE
	&ERRLIMIT = 1
	&ERRLIMIT = 0
	OUTPUT = 'errlimit=' &ERRLIMIT
	OUTPUT = 'still running'
END
```

```stdout
start
case=0
errlimit=0
still running
```

## fence_span_rpos_replace_branch_2

```SNOBOL4
*
*  FENCE FOLLOWED BY ONE MORE OPERAND, THEN AN ALTERNATION, IN A PATTERN HELD BY A VARIABLE:
*  SCRIP NEVER BACKTRACKS INTO THE ALTERNATION'S LATER ARMS.  Minted by cfo 2026-09-13 from
*  SPITBOL TEST PROGRAM #4's own GOTO_FIELD pattern, which is why the decomposed test4 entry
*  tpgm4_syntactic_recognizer is red on every statement carrying a two-part goto :S(A)F(B).
*  ARM Y1 is the defect: PV = ':' FENCE NULL (alt).  The first arm of the alternation matches a
*  PREFIX of the subject, RPOS(0) then fails, and the match must retry the second arm.
*  ARMS Y2, Y3 AND Y4 ARE THE CONTROLS AND THEY ISOLATE IT TO ONE PART EACH: Y2 drops the
*  operand between FENCE and the alternation, Y3 drops the FENCE, Y4 writes the SAME pattern
*  inline in the match statement instead of holding it in a variable.  All three are green in
*  SCRIP at the mint, so the class is all three together and none of them alone: A BARE FENCE,
*  AN ALTERNATION THAT IS NOT THE FIRST ELEMENT AFTER IT, AND THE WHOLE PATTERN REACHED THROUGH
*  A VARIABLE.  Measured with it and against it: FENCE alternation NULL is green, FENCE NULL
*  NULL alternation is red, and an element BEFORE the fence does not change either verdict, so
*  it is adjacency to the fence on the RIGHT that decides it.
*  ORACLE: /home/resources/x64/bin/sbl -bf matches all four.  REF CUT LIVE from it.
*
         &ANCHOR = 1
         G = '(' SPAN('AB') ')'
         S = ':S(A)F(B)'
         PV = ':' FENCE NULL ('S' G | 'S' G 'F' G)
         QV = ':' FENCE ('S' G | 'S' G 'F' G)
         RV = ':' NULL ('S' G | 'S' G 'F' G)
         S PV RPOS(0)                            :S(C1)F(D1)
C1       OUTPUT = 'Y1 FENCE OPERAND ALT IN A VARIABLE MATCH'    :(T2)
D1       OUTPUT = 'Y1 FENCE OPERAND ALT IN A VARIABLE FAIL'
T2       S QV RPOS(0)                            :S(C2)F(D2)
C2       OUTPUT = 'Y2 CONTROL FENCE THEN ALT MATCH'             :(T3)
D2       OUTPUT = 'Y2 CONTROL FENCE THEN ALT FAIL'
T3       S RV RPOS(0)                            :S(C3)F(D3)
C3       OUTPUT = 'Y3 CONTROL OPERAND THEN ALT MATCH'           :(T4)
D3       OUTPUT = 'Y3 CONTROL OPERAND THEN ALT FAIL'
T4       S ':' FENCE NULL ('S' G | 'S' G 'F' G) RPOS(0)         :S(C4)F(D4)
C4       OUTPUT = 'Y4 CONTROL SAME PATTERN INLINE MATCH'        :(END)
D4       OUTPUT = 'Y4 CONTROL SAME PATTERN INLINE FAIL'
END
```

```stdout
Y1 FENCE OPERAND ALT IN A VARIABLE MATCH
Y2 CONTROL FENCE THEN ALT MATCH
Y3 CONTROL OPERAND THEN ALT MATCH
Y4 CONTROL SAME PATTERN INLINE MATCH
```

```SNOBOL4
* A cursor (@A<1>) or an immediate capture ($ A<1>) whose target is an element or a call, held in an arm of an alternation or of FENCE, assigns that target: the pattern's head is found under the arm's own frame. A pattern with no
* conditional capture keeps its head on the stack, and the leaf in an arm read the slot the alternation's record covers; it was a SIGSEGV or a quiet no-op.
        DEFINE('H(N)')
        A = ARRAY(3)
        :(MAIN)
H       H = .V
        :(NRETURN)
MAIN    A[1] = 'x'
        A[2] = 'y'
        V = 'x'
        P = @A[1] | 'q'
        'abcdef' P
        OUTPUT = 'cur-alt ' A[1] ' ' A[2]
        A[1] = 'x'
        P = 'q' | @A[1]
        'abcdef' P
        OUTPUT = 'alt-cur ' A[1]
        A[1] = 'x'
        P = LEN(3) $ A[1] | 'q'
        'abcdef' P
        OUTPUT = 'imm-alt ' A[1]
        A[1] = 'x'
        P = FENCE(@A[1])
        'abcdef' P
        OUTPUT = 'cur-fence ' A[1]
        A[1] = 'x'
        P = FENCE(LEN(2) $ A[1])
        'abcdef' P
        OUTPUT = 'imm-fence ' A[1]
        A[1] = 'x'
        P = (@A[1] | 'q') | 'r'
        'abcdef' P
        OUTPUT = 'nested-alt ' A[1]
        A[1] = 'x'
        P = ('a' | @A[1]) @A[2]
        'abcdef' P
        OUTPUT = 'alt-then ' A[1] ' ' A[2]
        P = (LEN(3) @H(1)) | (LEN(1) @W)
        'abcdef' P
        OUTPUT = 'fn-cursor ' V
        V = 'x'
        P = FENCE(LEN(1) @H(1))
        'abcdef' P
        OUTPUT = 'fn-fence ' V
        V = 'x'
        P = @H(1) | 'q'
        'abcdef' P
        OUTPUT = 'fn-first ' V
END
```

```SNOBOL4
*     word4.sno - Record parsing using BREAKX instead of ARB.

*            while ARB succeeds with null. BREAKX is more precise for names.
*     Input format: YYYY  Name  : Invention  (same as word3)

+                 BREAKX(' ') . WHO (' ' SPAN(' :'))
+                 REM . WHAT
LOOP  LINE     =  INPUT                            :F(END)
      LINE     ?  PAT                              :F(LOOP)
      OUTPUT   =  WHO " invented the " WHAT " in " WHEN  :(LOOP)
END
```

```stdin
1903  Wright : Airplane
1928  Fleming : Penicillin
```

## user_function_arbno_span_replace_branch_2

```SNOBOL4
* rty_arbno_extend_double_fires_cond_capture -- FALSIFICATION WITNESS (hq_C, s261)
* A deferred conditional capture ( . *FN() ) whose captured sub-pattern contains an
* ARBNO that EXTENDS after the capture's first success fires its action TWICE:
* once at the premature shorter extent, once at the final extent.
* Oracle prints P P P A ; the defect prints P P A P A (one extra A).
* Minimal: the INNER capture is NOT required -- ARBNO alone, uncaptured, is enough.
* Mechanism: bb_match_capture.cpp IR_MATCH_CAPTURE_COND appends the pend entry at
* alpha (add r12,24) and retracts it ONLY on the beta->omega concede path; an ARBNO
* extension re-enters alpha without ever conceding, so the first entry is never
* retracted and rt_dcap_pump replays it.  Same family as rung-arbno-selfloop.
        DEFINE('P()')                           :(P_end)
P       OUTPUT = 'P'
        P = .dm                                 :(NRETURN)
P_end
        DEFINE('A()')                           :(A_end)
A       OUTPUT = 'A'
        A = .dm                                 :(NRETURN)
A_end
        F = SPAN('0123456789') . *P()
        T = F ARBNO('*' F)
        X = T ARBNO('+' T . *A())
        C = POS(0) X RPOS(0)
        '1+2*3' C                               :S(y)F(n)
y       OUTPUT = 'ok'                           :(END)
n       OUTPUT = 'no'
END
```

## bal_span_pos_replace_branch_2

```SNOBOL4
*  leafsib bal flat grn -- s193 (row alt-arb-bal-witness).  THE ALT-ARM LEAF-SUSPENSION CLASS
*  FOR BAL, minted in the PADDED shape of probe/cn/cn_alt_leaf_flat_grn because this family's
*  own leafsib_bal.sno has gone INERT: on the STORED road (`t = (... | BAL . I)`) its cell is
*  already [rbp-96] on BOTH killswitch arms, so it is green for a reason unrelated to the switch
*  it exists to test, and its --compile output is byte-identical across the two arms.
*  Here the alternation is INLINE, so the BAL suspension cell is a RAW FLAT ZLS COORDINATE off
*  rsp (LFC legacy arm).  Only the padding count differs across this pair -- the pattern is the
*  same -- which is what proves the defect is the COORDINATE'S MAGNITUDE and never the shape.
*  Five padding assignments leave it at [rsp+224], still INSIDE the live frame, so the program is
*  green on BOTH arms in BOTH media.  A green here is LUCK, not correctness -- it is the control
*  that dates the red twin's crash to the coordinate and not to BAL.
*  BAL SEMANTICS (SPITBOL v3.7 p.207): BAL carries IMPLICIT alternatives tried BEFORE explicit
*  ones, extending to the next-shortest balanced string (p.124: shortest non-null string in which
*  parentheses are balanced; a string without parentheses is balanced).  Its beta resumes an
*  ADVANCING SCAN through a suspension cursor, which is what makes it a scratch-cell leaf.
*  BAL is the sibling that spends THREE words, LFC(0)/LFC(4)/LFC(8) -- visible in the emitted asm
*  as [rsp+464]/[rsp+468]/[rsp+472] -- the s131 decline reason, covered since s174 by the
*  TWO-CONSECUTIVE-SLOT registry claim (44b8b82c).
	V1 = "pad1"
	V2 = "pad2"
	V3 = "pad3"
	V4 = "pad4"
	V5 = "pad5"
	"ab" POS(0) (BAL | SPAN("09")) RPOS(0)	:S(Y)F(N)
Y	OUTPUT = "match"	:(END)
N	OUTPUT = "nomatch"
END
```

```stdout
match
```

## user_function_code_eval_array_replace_branch_1

```SNOBOL4
*  seq_code_loop_in_function - distilled from gimpel SEQ_driver (batch C);
*  the same crash takes AI_driver and AOPA_driver, which both go through SEQ.
*  A DEFINE'd function that (a) reaches its loop variable INDIRECTLY through
*  a name argument, (b) drives a CODE()-compiled statement with an indirect
*  goto :<ARG_S>, and (c) returns after that loop finally fails, runs the
*  loop body correctly -- a, b, c below -- and then SEGFAULTS on the way out.
*  Oracle (sbl -b) prints a, b, c, then "K = 4".  SCRIP prints a, b, c and
*  dies with SIGSEGV in BOTH m3 and m4.
*  BOTH INGREDIENTS ARE NEEDED, and each half is correct on its own:
*    - the CODE loop with :<C> at top level, exiting on failure, is right
*      (see the L1/L2 loop below, which prints "exited with K = 4");
*    - a function that writes and reads its caller's variable through
*      $ARG_NAME and then FRETURNs is right (see F1 below).
*  Only the two together crash, so this is not "CODE is unimplemented" --
*  CODE, :<VAR> and indirect name arguments each work.
        DEFINE('S1(ARG_S,ARG_NAME)')            :(S1_END)
S1      $ARG_NAME  =  0
        ARG_S  =  CODE(ARG_S ' :S(S1_1)F(S1_2)')        :F(ERROR)
S1_1    $ARG_NAME  =  $ARG_NAME + 1             :<ARG_S>
S1_2    EQ($ARG_NAME,1)                         :S(FRETURN)F(RETURN)
S1_END
        DEFINE('F1(ARG_NAME)')                  :(F1_END)
F1      $ARG_NAME  =  0
        $ARG_NAME  =  $ARG_NAME + 1
        EQ($ARG_NAME,1)                         :S(FRETURN)F(RETURN)
F1_END
        A  =  ARRAY(3)
        A[1]  =  'a'
        A[2]  =  'b'
        A[3]  =  'c'
        C  =  CODE(' OUTPUT = A[J] :S(L1)F(L2)')
        J  =  0
L1      J  =  J + 1                             :<C>
L2      OUTPUT  =  'sibling CODE loop exited with J = ' J
        F1(.M)                                  :F(SIB2)
        OUTPUT  =  'sibling function returned, M = ' M    :(WITNESS)
SIB2    OUTPUT  =  'sibling function freturned, M = ' M
WITNESS S1(' OUTPUT = A[K] ', .K)
        OUTPUT  =  'witness returned, K = ' K
END
```

```stdout
a
b
c
sibling CODE loop exited with J = 4
sibling function freturned, M = 1
a
b
c
witness returned, K = 4
```

## len_table_array_replace_branch_1

```SNOBOL4
*     indirect_name_boundary.sno -- THE UNARY $ ACCEPT/REFUSE BOUNDARY, ERROR 239.
*     Manual v3.7 p.83: "Indirection may proceed to any depth, provided the null
*     string is never encountered as a variable name" -- the null string is not a
*     valid variable name and SPITBOL answers ERROR 239.  p.196: $(.A) is the same
*     as using variable A, so a NAME operand needs no conversion at all.
*     &ERRLIMIT converts each error to statement failure (Ch.16), so the code
*     arrives as ordinary output on the :F branch and the oracle prints no banner.
*     The final &ERRLIMIT line is the corroborating count: one credit per refusal.
        &ERRLIMIT = 1000
        ABC = 'legal'
        A = $'ABC'                      :F(F1)
        OUTPUT = 'T1 ok ' A             :(T2)
F1      OUTPUT = 'T1 ERR ' &ERRTYPE
T2      B = $UNSET                      :F(F2)
        OUTPUT = 'T2 ok'                :(T3)
F2      OUTPUT = 'T2 ERR ' &ERRTYPE
T3      C = $''                         :F(F3)
        OUTPUT = 'T3 ok'                :(T4)
F3      OUTPUT = 'T3 ERR ' &ERRTYPE
T4      $'=' = 'eq'
        D = $'='                        :F(F4)
        OUTPUT = 'T4 ok ' D             :(T5)
F4      OUTPUT = 'T4 ERR ' &ERRTYPE
T5      E = $3                          :F(F5)
        OUTPUT = 'T5 ok'                :(T6)
F5      OUTPUT = 'T5 ERR ' &ERRTYPE
T6      F = $0                          :F(F6)
        OUTPUT = 'T6 ok'                :(T7)
F6      OUTPUT = 'T6 ERR ' &ERRTYPE
T7      G = $3.5                        :F(F7)
        OUTPUT = 'T7 ok'                :(T8)
F7      OUTPUT = 'T7 ERR ' &ERRTYPE
T8      H = $ARRAY(3)                   :F(F8)
        OUTPUT = 'T8 ok'                :(T9)
F8      OUTPUT = 'T8 ERR ' &ERRTYPE
T9      I = $TABLE()                    :F(F9)
        OUTPUT = 'T9 ok'                :(TA)
F9      OUTPUT = 'T9 ERR ' &ERRTYPE
TA      J = $(.ABC)                     :F(FA)
        OUTPUT = 'TA ok ' J             :(TB)
FA      OUTPUT = 'TA ERR ' &ERRTYPE
TB      K = $(LEN(1))                   :F(FB)
        OUTPUT = 'TB ok'                :(TC)
FB      OUTPUT = 'TB ERR ' &ERRTYPE
TC      OUTPUT = 'END errlimit=' &ERRLIMIT
END
```

## test_smoke_expr_parser

```SNOBOL4
* expr_parser.sno — Expression parser in SNOBOL4
* Translated mechanically from Expressions.py (ByrdBox)
* Each Python generator function becomes a named SNOBOL4 pattern
*
* parse_item:
*   SPAN('0123456789') | 'x' | 'y' | 'z' | '(' parse_term ')'
*
* parse_element:
*   parse_item | '+' parse_element | '-' parse_element
*
* parse_factor:
*   parse_element | parse_element '*' parse_factor | parse_element '/' parse_factor
*
* parse_term:
*   parse_factor | parse_factor '+' parse_term | parse_factor '-' parse_term
*
* parse_expression:
*   POS(0) parse_term RPOS(0)

        DEFINE('ITEM()')
        DEFINE('ELEMENT()')
        DEFINE('FACTOR()')
        DEFINE('TERM()')
        DEFINE('EXPRESSION()')

* ── ITEM ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ITEM    SUBJECT SPAN('0123456789')          :S(ITEM.OK)
        SUBJECT LIT('x')                    :S(ITEM.OK)
        SUBJECT LIT('y')                    :S(ITEM.OK)
        SUBJECT LIT('z')                    :S(ITEM.OK)
        SUBJECT LIT('(')                    :F(ITEM.FAIL)
        TERM()                              :F(ITEM.FAIL)
        SUBJECT LIT(')')                    :F(ITEM.FAIL)
ITEM.OK                                     :(RETURN)
ITEM.FAIL                                   :F(FRETURN)

* ── ELEMENT ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ELEMENT ITEM()                              :S(ELEMENT.OK)
        SUBJECT LIT('+')                    :F(ELEMENT.TRY.MINUS)
        ELEMENT()                           :S(ELEMENT.OK) F(ELEMENT.TRY.MINUS)
ELEMENT.TRY.MINUS
        SUBJECT LIT('-')                    :F(ELEMENT.FAIL)
        ELEMENT()                           :S(ELEMENT.OK) F(ELEMENT.FAIL)
ELEMENT.OK                                  :(RETURN)
ELEMENT.FAIL                                :(FRETURN)

END
```

```SNOBOL4
ListEnd
        s = list()
        ListAppend(s, list())
        OUTPUT = 'after1 n=' n(s) ' proto=' PROTOTYPE(a(s))
        ListAppend(s, list())
        OUTPUT = 'after2 n=' n(s) ' proto=' PROTOTYPE(a(s))
        ListAppend(s, list())
        OUTPUT = 'after3 n=' n(s) ' proto=' PROTOTYPE(a(s))
END
```

## any_pos_rpos_replace_branch_1

```SNOBOL4
*------------------------------------------------------------------------------
* alt_defer_recur_af.sno — RED witness (s101).  A recursive deferred pattern
* through an ALT arm: the ALT's all-fail edge reads a saved cursor cell that
* holds a DEFER RESUME ADDRESS, so the cursor becomes a code address, every
* later box fails (cursor >> subject end) and the match SPINS FOREVER.
*
*     A  =  V | '(' *A ')'        second arm defers back into the same pattern
*
* SCRIP prints MATCHED 1/2/3 then HANGS on the 4th (the FAILING match — the
* one that actually takes the af edge).  Oracle prints all four lines in well
* under a second.  Reproduces in m3 and m4.
*
* MEASURED (m4, gdb, s101):
*   - the ALT carves 32B at alpha {cursor+0, beta resume+8, af resume+16, pad}
*     and af does  mov r14d,[rsp+0]  /  mov rax,[rsp+16]; jmp rax
*   - while spinning on calculator-1-match.sno, r14 = 0x402495 = the ADDRESS
*     of n30_match_defer_beta, and [rsp+0] held that same code address
*   - r15 (subject length) and r12 (arena) were correct throughout, and rsp
*     was STABLE — this is a non-progressing spin, NOT runaway recursion
*
* ⛔ FALSIFIED, DO NOT RE-CHASE (s101): "the af edge runs at the wrong DEPTH".
* An interleaved alpha/af rsp trace over one run (gdb, breakpoints on both
* labels, 14 stops) shows every af executing exactly 32 bytes below its own
* alpha — i.e. AT its own post-carve depth, self-consistent at every recursion
* level.  The first measurement that suggested otherwise (alpha 0x7fffffffe890
* vs af 0x7fffffffe450, "1088 bytes deeper") compared TWO DIFFERENT RECURSION
* INSTANCES and is void — the RULES.md "passing sibling is not evidence"
* trap in its depth spelling.
*
* SO THE HUNT IS: who WRITES the ALT's saved-cursor cell after alpha stored it?
* Prime suspect class is a store at a computed, un-rebased [rsp+K] that ALIASES
* another construct's carve — the s99/s100 flat-coordinate family (e.g. the
* `mov qword ptr [rsp + 16], rax` defer-record store seen beside the defer
* alpha in calculator-1-match.s at line 475, which moves NO rsp).  HW
* watchpoints do not work in this container: convict with a breakpoint on each
* candidate store conditioned on the effective address, or an ignore-count spin
* to the exact instance, per RULES.md MONITOR-FIRST step (2).
*
*
* ⭐ ROOT CAUSE CONVICTED (s101, gdb, this witness): the 32 bytes the ALT reads
* as its carve are a BLOB GAMMA-SUSPENSION RECORD.  Conditional breakpoint
*   break n3_match_alternate_af if *(int*)$rsp > 100000
* stops with rsp=0x7fffffffe830 and the quad:
*   [rsp+ 0] = proc_PAT$1_res        (blob resume entry)
*   [rsp+ 8] = n6_match_defer_alpha+134   (r10 / gamma wire)
*   [rsp+16] = n6_match_defer_alpha+139   (r11 / omega wire)
*   [rsp+24] = 0x7fffffffe8a8             (saved rbp)
* i.e. exactly the CLASS D {res, r10, r11, rbp} record of the s97 R-4(b)
* blob-activation design — same 32-byte size as the ALT carve, sitting at the
* ALT's carve address.  So a blob activation's whack RELEASED spine memory the
* live enclosing ALT still owns, and the next gamma suspension reused it; the
* ALT then reads res as its cursor (a code address) and spins.  Spine
* use-after-free, not a depth-formula error (see FALSIFIED above).
*
* CURE DIRECTION (matches Lon's s95 ruling + the landed R-4(f) FENCE1
* precedent): an ALT whose arm can suspend an activation cannot keep its
* {cursor, beta, af} cells on the spine at all — they want ACTIVATION-FRAME
* SLOTS via the shared frame_slot_scan registry (alt_frame_candidate ->
* alt_frame_slot -> op_alt_frame_off, mirroring fence_frame_candidate /
* fence_frame_slot / op_fence_frame_off, emit.cpp:732/2311, template
* bb_match_fence1.cpp:51/61).  Static arms keep the RSP quads byte-identical.
*
* Owns (same class, to be re-measured against this witness once it is green):
* demos TIMEOUT block calculator-1-match / calculator-2* / json-match* (6 rows,
* all recursive deferred grammars).
*------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        V              =  ANY('abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz')
        A              =  V | '(' *A ')'
        P              =  POS(0) A RPOS(0)
*------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        S1             =  'x'
        S2             =  '(y)'
        S3             =  '((z))'
        S4             =  '(w'
*------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        S1  P                                                                  :F(F1)
        OUTPUT         =  'MATCHED 1'                                          :(T2)
F1      OUTPUT         =  'NOMATCH 1'
T2      S2  P                                                                  :F(F2)
        OUTPUT         =  'MATCHED 2'                                          :(T3)
F2      OUTPUT         =  'NOMATCH 2'
T3      S3  P                                                                  :F(F3)
        OUTPUT         =  'MATCHED 3'                                          :(T4)
F3      OUTPUT         =  'NOMATCH 3'
T4      S4  P                                                                  :F(F4)
        OUTPUT         =  'MATCHED 4'                                          :(DONE)
F4      OUTPUT         =  'NOMATCH 4'
DONE
END
```

## benchmark_eval_fixed

```SNOBOL4
* eval_fixed -- compiles and evaluates the expression 'X + 1' at run time, N times.
* bottleneck: run-time compilation of a fixed expression string.
* Standalone:  scrip eval_fixed.sno   |   sbl -bf eval_fixed.sno   |   snobol4 eval_fixed.sno

        &ANCHOR = 0
        &STLIMIT = -1

        DEFINE('EVAL_FIXED(N)')                         :(EVAL_FIXED_END)
EVAL_FIXED  ZI = 1
```

```SNOBOL4
	DEFINE(NAME  ARGS)			:(RETURN)

	N = 'FOO'
```

## arb_span_pos_replace_branch_2

```SNOBOL4
*  leafsib arb flat grn -- s193 (row alt-arb-bal-witness).  THE ALT-ARM LEAF-SUSPENSION CLASS
*  FOR ARB, minted in the PADDED shape of probe/cn/cn_alt_leaf_flat_grn because this family's
*  own leafsib_arb.sno has gone INERT: on the STORED road (`t = (... | ARB . I)`) its cell is
*  already [rbp-96] on BOTH killswitch arms, so it is green for a reason unrelated to the switch
*  it exists to test, and its --compile output is byte-identical across the two arms.
*  Here the alternation is INLINE, so the ARB suspension cell is a RAW FLAT ZLS COORDINATE off
*  rsp (LFC legacy arm).  Only the padding count differs across this pair -- the pattern is the
*  same -- which is what proves the defect is the COORDINATE'S MAGNITUDE and never the shape.
*  Five padding assignments leave it at [rsp+240], still INSIDE the live frame, so the program is
*  green on BOTH arms in BOTH media.  A green here is LUCK, not correctness -- it is the control
*  that dates the red twin's crash to the coordinate and not to ARB.
*  ARB SEMANTICS (SPITBOL v3.7 p.207): ARB carries IMPLICIT alternatives tried BEFORE explicit
*  ones -- it behaves as (LEN(0) | LEN(1) | LEN(2) | ...) -- so its beta resumes an ADVANCING
*  SCAN through a suspension cursor.  That resume is what makes it a scratch-cell leaf.
	V1 = "pad1"
	V2 = "pad2"
	V3 = "pad3"
	V4 = "pad4"
	V5 = "pad5"
	"ab" POS(0) (ARB | SPAN("09")) RPOS(0)	:S(Y)F(N)
Y	OUTPUT = "match"	:(END)
N	OUTPUT = "nomatch"
END
```

```stdout
match
```

```SNOBOL4
Y1      'xy' &SUCCEED . V
```

## break_len_table_replace_branch_1

```SNOBOL4
* A pattern stored in a variable binds an array or table element's NAME when it is built, as SPITBOL does: . A[2], $ T['k'], @A[1], the
* loop-built PAT[I] = LEN(1) . A[I], a name read at construction and not at match, and an out-of-range subscript that fails the statement.
	arr = ARRAY(3)
	tbl = TABLE()
	pats = ARRAY(2)
	cnd = 'y' . arr[2]
	'xyz' cnd
	imm = BREAK('z') $ tbl['k']
	'xyz' imm
	cur = @arr[1] 'y'
	'xyz' cur
	OUTPUT = 'A1=' arr[1] ' A2=' arr[2] ' A3=' arr[3] ' Tk=' tbl['k']
	idx = 1
build	pats[idx] = LEN(1) . arr[idx]
	idx = LT(idx,2) idx + 1	:S(build)
	'q' pats[2]
	'r' pats[1]
	OUTPUT = 'A1=' arr[1] ' A2=' arr[2] ' A3=' arr[3]
	idx = 1
	bound = LEN(1) $ arr[idx]
	idx = 3
	'w' bound
	OUTPUT = 'A1=' arr[1] ' A3=' arr[3]
	oor = 'y' . arr[7]	:S(built)F(refused)
built	OUTPUT = 'built'	:(done)
refused	OUTPUT = 'refused'
done	oor = 'ok'
	OUTPUT = oor
END
```

```stdout
A1=r A2=q A3=
A1=w A3=
refused
ok
```

## notany_convert_datatype_replace_1

```SNOBOL4
* SPITBOL has no function REAL (the data type is spelled in DATATYPE and CONVERT only), so a call of REAL is an undefined function: error 22, in a plain statement and in every place a pattern is built, an alternation arm included
* (all the function calls of a pattern are made as it is built, before the match). A DATA field named REAL is its own function and still works.
        &ERRLIMIT = 100
        V = 'none'
        V = REAL(1E300)
        OUTPUT = 'a ' &ERRTYPE ' ' V
        &ERRTYPE = 0
        V = IDENT(REAL(1E300))
        OUTPUT = 'b ' &ERRTYPE ' ' V
        &ERRTYPE = 0
        V = 'none'
        V = REPLACE(REAL(SIZE('4z')), &LCASE, &UCASE)
        OUTPUT = 'c ' &ERRTYPE ' ' V
        &ERRTYPE = 0
        V = 'none'
        V = 'abc' ? NOTANY('x') . Y | NE(3, 8) IDENT(REAL(1E300))
        OUTPUT = 'arm ' &ERRTYPE ' ' V
        &ERRTYPE = 0
        V = 'none'
        V = 'abc' ? 'a' | REAL(1)
        OUTPUT = 'alt ' &ERRTYPE ' ' V
        &ERRTYPE = 0
        P = 'a' | REAL(1)
        OUTPUT = 'value ' &ERRTYPE ' ' DATATYPE(P)
        &ERRTYPE = 0
        V = 'abc' ? REAL(1) @Z
        OUTPUT = 'cursor ' &ERRTYPE
        &ERRTYPE = 0
        V = 'none'
        V = 'abc' ? 'a' REAL(1)
        OUTPUT = 'seq ' &ERRTYPE ' ' V
        &ERRTYPE = 0
        DATA('COMPLEX(REAL,IMAG)')
        X = COMPLEX(3.2, 2.0)
        OUTPUT = 'field ' &ERRTYPE ' ' REAL(X) ' ' IMAG(X)
END
```

```SNOBOL4
        &ERRTYPE = 0

        X = EVAL('"p' CHAR(10) 'q"')

        E = CONVERT("'u" CHAR(10) "v'", 'EXPRESSION')
        OUTPUT = 'convert-lf ' DATATYPE(E) ' ' SIZE(EVAL(E))
        X = EVAL("'a" CHAR(13) "b'")
        OUTPUT = 'eval-cr ' SIZE(X)
        &ERRTYPE = 0
        D = 'none'
        D = CODE('END')
        OUTPUT = 'code-end0 ' &ERRTYPE ' ' DATATYPE(D)
        &ERRTYPE = 0
        D = 'none'
        D = CODE("END; OUTPUT = 'never'")
        OUTPUT = 'code-end1 ' &ERRTYPE ' ' DATATYPE(D)
        &ERRTYPE = 0

        &ERRTYPE = 0
```

```SNOBOL4
        &TRIM = 1
```

```SNOBOL4
        S = REPLACE(S, 'aeiou', '*****')
        NS = SIZE(S)
        ZI = LT(ZI, N) ZI + 1                           :S(ZBL)
        STRING_MANIP = NS                               :(RETURN)
STRING_MANIP_END

END
```

```SNOBOL4
      &TRIM    =  1

      PRINTV   =  V

PRINT PRINTV   ?  LEN(1) . C =                     :F(NEXTV)
      OUTPUT   =  DIFFER(C, '#') DUPL(' ', NH) C   :S(PRINT)
      OUTPUT   =  H                                :(PRINT)
END
```

## benchmark_name_indirection

```SNOBOL4
* name_indirection -- repeatedly reads and writes a variable through a runtime-computed name.
* bottleneck: $-indirection's by-name dispatch chain (rt_call_arr_bl -> try_call_builtin_by_name_bl -> bn_sno_name),
* the mechanism perf-dispatch-fastpath-name-indirect targets. holder never becomes a compile-time-known literal
* name at the $ site, so the s266 .VAR-over-a-literal fold (lower_snobol4.c) cannot short-circuit this loop.
* Standalone:  scrip name_indirection.sno   |   sbl -bf name_indirection.sno   |   snobol4 name_indirection.sno
        &TRIM = 1
        &ANCHOR = 0
        &STLIMIT = -1
        DEFINE('name_indirection(n)')                   :(name_indirection_end)
name_indirection    target = 0
        holder = 'target'
        counter = 1
indirect_loop    $holder = $holder + 1
        counter = LT(counter, n) counter + 1            :S(indirect_loop)
        name_indirection = $holder                       :(RETURN)
name_indirection_end
*BENCH kernel=name_indirection check=20000 bud=500 flr=20
        OUTPUT = 'final value = ' name_indirection(20000)
END
```

```stdout
final value = 20000
```

```SNOBOL4
        S = " Y = +.X"                                       :(TRY)
R1      S = " Y = -.X"                                       :(TRY)

R3      S = " Y = .X * 2"                                    :(TRY)
R4      S = " Y = .&ERRTEXT 'z'"                             :(TRY)
R5      S = " Y = 'z' .&ERRTEXT"                             :(TRY)
R6      S = " Y = LEN(.X)"                                   :(TRY)
R7      S = " Y = SIZE(.&ERRTEXT)"                           :(TRY)
R8      S = " Y = ANY(.&ERRTEXT)"                            :(TRY)
R9      S = " Y = .*X + 1"                                   :(TRY)
R10      S = " Y = @X + 1"                                   :(TRY)
R11      S = " Y = .X 'l'"                                   :(TRY)
R12      S = " Y = .A[1] + 1"                                :(TRY)
R13      S = " Y = .F() + 1"                                 :(TRY)
R14                                                          :(END)
TRY     N = N + 1
        CODE(S)                                              :F(BAD)
        OUTPUT = 'compiled: ' S                              :($('R' N))
BAD     OUTPUT = &ERRTYPE ': ' S                             :($('R' N))
END
```

## ladder__rung07_inf_dotnet_an_element_holding_an_expression_is_assigned_itself

```SNOBOL4
* An element, a table entry or a field that holds an expression is itself the target of = and of . and $ in a pattern, as a
* variable that holds one is; only a deferred expression written as the target is evaluated for its name (rung07, arrays)
        N = 'o'
        A = ARRAY(2)
        A[1] = *N
        A[1] = 'm'
        OUTPUT = '1 N=' N ' A1=' DATATYPE(A[1]) ' ' A[1]
        T = TABLE()
        T['k'] = *N
        T['k'] = 'm'
        OUTPUT = '2 N=' N ' Tk=' T['k']
        DATA('PT(U,V)')
        G = PT(CONVERT('N', 'EXPRESSION'), 1)
        U(G) = 'm'
        OUTPUT = '3 N=' N ' U=' U(G)
        A[1] = *N
        'abc' ? LEN(1) . A[1]
        OUTPUT = '4 N=' N ' A1=' A[1]
        A[1] = *N
        'abc' ? LEN(2) $ A[1]
        OUTPUT = '5 N=' N ' A1=' A[1]
        'abc' ? LEN(1) . *N
        OUTPUT = '6 N=' N
END
```

```SNOBOL4
+              (CONVERT(.*SIZE(X), 'STRING'), 'no text')
END
```

## code_eval_array_datatype_replace_branch_1

```SNOBOL4
*     indirect_name_datatypes.sno -- WHICH DATATYPES $ REFUSES, AND THE LHS AND
*     DOUBLE-INDIRECTION POSITIONS.  Every refusal here is ERROR 239 on the live
*     oracle; each spends exactly one &ERRLIMIT credit, which the closing line
*     counts.  $3.5 is admitted and names the variable literally called 3.5 --
*     round-tripped through $'3.5' so the accept half is pinned by value, not by
*     the absence of an error.
*     ⛔ NO CODE-OBJECT LINE HERE ON PURPOSE: the oracle refuses $CODE(...) with 239,
*     but SCRIP's CODE() answers DATATYPE STRING (measured), so such a line would
*     pass for the wrong reason.  EXPRESSION and the DATA object carry that half,
*     and DATATYPE agrees with the oracle on both (PT / EXPRESSION, measured).
        &ERRLIMIT = 1000
        DATA('PT(XX,YY)')
        P = PT(1,2)
        A = $P                          :F(F1)
        OUTPUT = 'T1 ok DATA'           :(T2)
F1      OUTPUT = 'T1 ERR ' &ERRTYPE
T2      Q = *(1 + 1)
        B = $Q                          :F(F2)
        OUTPUT = 'T2 ok EXPR'           :(T3)
F2      OUTPUT = 'T2 ERR ' &ERRTYPE
T3      $UNSET1 = 'x'                   :F(F3)
        OUTPUT = 'T3 ok LHSNULL'        :(T4)
F3      OUTPUT = 'T3 ERR ' &ERRTYPE
T4      $ARRAY(2) = 'x'                 :F(F4)
        OUTPUT = 'T4 ok LHSARR'         :(T5)
F4      OUTPUT = 'T4 ERR ' &ERRTYPE
T5      OUTPUT = $UNSET2                :F(F5)
        OUTPUT = 'T5 ok OUTNULL'        :(T6)
F5      OUTPUT = 'T5 ERR ' &ERRTYPE
T6      D = $$UNSET3                    :F(F6)
        OUTPUT = 'T6 ok DBL'            :(T7)
F6      OUTPUT = 'T6 ERR ' &ERRTYPE
T7      E = $(1 - 1)                    :F(F7)
        OUTPUT = 'T7 ok ZERO'           :(T8)
F7      OUTPUT = 'T7 ERR ' &ERRTYPE
T8      $3.5 = 'realname'
        G = $'3.5'                      :F(F8)
        OUTPUT = 'T8 realname=' G       :(T9)
F8      OUTPUT = 'T8 ERR ' &ERRTYPE
T9      OUTPUT = 'END errlimit=' &ERRLIMIT
END
```

```stdout
T1 ERR 239
T2 ERR 239
T3 ERR 239
T4 ERR 239
T5 ERR 239
T6 ERR 239
T7 ok ZERO
T8 realname=realname
END errlimit=994
```
